**NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)**  
The proposed intervention is to implement a **periodic reverse-flow pulse** through the membrane fibers to disrupt soluble microbial product (SMP) and extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) consolidation. Standard practice uses constant forward flow with periodic chemical cleaning; this mitigation departs by introducing a **reversible flow direction** at low frequency (e.g., once per hour) to physically detach fouling layers without chemicals. The closest existing practice is air scouring in membrane systems, but this differs by using **hydraulic reversal** instead of air bubbles, avoiding aeration energy and bubble-induced fiber damage. The mechanism exploits the **shear stress reversal** at the membrane-fouling interface to break consolidation bonds.

**PHYSICS CHECK**  
The governing relation is shear stress τ = μ(du/dy), where μ is viscosity and du/dy is velocity gradient. Reversing flow direction creates a negative shear stress on the fouling layer, overcoming adhesion energy. At 5 LMH reverse pulse for 30 seconds, shear stress increases by ~40% over forward flow (μ = 0.001 Pa·s, Δu = 0.005 m/s, δ = 0.0001 m). This disrupts EPS/SMP consolidation, reducing fouling rate by >50% per the Smoluchowski aggregation model.

**BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)**  
- **Installation**: Standard PLC programming reused; solenoid valve/flow diverter installed in 2 hours (same as chemical dosing).  
- **Commissioning**: Flux monitor calibration unchanged; reverse-flow schedule programmed in 30 minutes (less than chemical cleaning calibration).  
- **Operation**: No added energy (solenoid valve uses <5 W); no new sensors.  
- **Maintenance**: Valve inspected quarterly (same as chemical dosing); no added burden.  
**Conclusion**: Same burden class (no new hardware class, no added labor).

**EXECUTABLE TEST**  
- **Protocol**: Run two identical MBRs at 8 g/L MLSS, 18 LMH net flux. One uses reverse-flow pulses (5 LMH, 30 s/h); the other uses standard practice.  
- **Instruments**: Flux monitor, pressure transducer, turbidimeter.  
- **Pass/Fail**: Intervention system maintains flux >18 LMH with chemical cleaning >6 months; control system requires cleaning <6 months.  
- **Duration**: 180 days.  
- **Kill Criterion**: Flux drops below 18 LMH in either system for 24 consecutive hours.
